content.text: higher than recommended doses and IV use appear to carry a higher risk of QTc prolongation and torsades; a QTc over 500 msec raises torsades risk. The inj = ⍉approved for IV use; if given IV, monitor the ECG for QTc prolongation and arrhythmias.

caution w other QTc-prolonging drugs (eg, Class 1A and Class 3 antiarrhythmics, citalopram, erythromycin, levofloxacin, methadone, ziprasidone) and w drugs causing lyte imbalance (eg, diuretics, corticosteroids). Potent CYP3A4 inducers (eg, carbamazepine, phenobarbital, phenytoin, RIF, St John's wort) may lower haloperidol levels enough to reduce efficacy. W lithium, an encephalopathic syndrome followed by irreversible brain damage has occurred in a few pts.

mainly severe EPS, hypotension or sedation; consider the risk of ECG chgs assoc w torsades. ⍉specific antidote, so tx = supportive; dialysis isn't recommended. For hypotension use IVF, plasma or albumin and vasopressors (eg, phenylephrine, NE); Epi must ⍉be used. Give antiparkinson med for severe EPS, and monitor the ECG until it = norm.

sources.name: Haloperidol injection, USP prescribing information (FDA label, DailyMed)
